title_th: มอเตอร์ไซค์รับจ้างและรถสองแถว
recycles: clarification: 'Sorry, could you say that again?'
register: Casual-polite street register — short, friendly, spoken over engine noise; first-name-free, no honorifics needed

targets.why_it_matters_here: The fare is agreed by voice, before you get on, with the engine running. If your 'thirty' lands as 'thirteen', the driver stops halfway and argues; if you hear 'fifty' when he said 'fifteen', you hand over three times the fare and get no change back. Stress the first syllable for -ty and release the final -n for -teen.

Stopping instructions are one or two words long, shouted forward over an engine. A swallowed final /p/ in 'stop' or /ft/ in 'left' means the driver keeps going and you are dropped a kilometre past your street, in the dark, paying extra to come back. Release the last sound — that final consonant is the whole message.

model_dialogues.label: Motorbike taxi — agree the fare, then stop where you want

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Excuse me, how much to the train station?
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ ไปสถานีรถไฟเท่าไหร่?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Sixty baht.
lines.th: หกสิบบาท

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sixty, not sixteen?
lines.th: หกสิบ ไม่ใช่สิบหกใช่ไหม?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Sixty. Six-zero.
lines.th: หกสิบ หก-ศูนย์

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay. Do you have a helmet?
lines.th: โอเค มีหมวกกันน็อคไหม?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Yeah, here you go. Hop on.
lines.th: มี นี่เลย ขึ้นมาได้

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Please stop at the front gate.
lines.th: ขอจอดตรงหน้าประตูนะ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: No problem. … Okay, the front gate.
lines.th: ได้เลย … เอ้า ถึงหน้าประตูแล้ว

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thanks. Here's sixty baht.
lines.th: ขอบคุณ นี่หกสิบบาท

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Thanks. Have a good trip.
lines.th: ขอบคุณ เดินทางปลอดภัยนะ

model_dialogues.label: Songthaew — waiting for passengers, a closed road, and no change

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Where are you going?
lines.th: จะไปไหนเหรอ?

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: To the old market. How much?
lines.th: ไปตลาดเก่า เท่าไหร่?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Thirty each. Get in the back.
lines.th: คนละสามสิบ ขึ้นข้างหลังเลย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Thirty each, right?
lines.th: คนละสามสิบใช่ไหม?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Right, thirty. But we wait — I need two more people.
lines.th: ใช่ สามสิบ แต่ขอรอก่อนนะ ขออีกสองคน

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, how long? Five or fifteen?
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ รอนานไหม? ห้านาทีหรือสิบห้านาที?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Five minutes. No more than five.
lines.th: ห้านาที ไม่เกินห้านาที

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Okay, I'll wait.
lines.th: โอเค งั้นรอ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Right, we're off. … Ah — the road at the bridge is closed today.
lines.th: เอาละ ไปละ … อ้าว วันนี้ถนนตรงสะพานปิด

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, could you say that again?
lines.th: ขอโทษ พูดอีกทีได้ไหม?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: I can't reach the market. I stop at the temple, then you walk.
lines.th: เข้าตลาดไม่ได้ ผมจอดที่วัด แล้วคุณเดินต่อเอานะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: How far is the walk?
lines.th: ต้องเดินไกลไหม?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Four hundred metres. Straight ahead, then left at the corner.
lines.th: สี่ร้อยเมตร ตรงไปแล้วเลี้ยวซ้ายตรงหัวมุม

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Straight ahead, then left. Got it.
lines.th: ตรงไป แล้วเลี้ยวซ้าย เข้าใจแล้ว

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Okay — the temple. Stop here?
lines.th: เอ้า ถึงวัดแล้ว จอดตรงนี้นะ?

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Yes, stop here, please.
lines.th: ใช่ จอดตรงนี้เลย

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Sorry, I only have a hundred.
lines.th: ขอโทษนะ ผมมีแต่แบงค์ร้อย

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: A hundred? I've only got twenty in change.
lines.th: ร้อยเหรอ? มีเงินทอนแค่ยี่สิบเองนะ

lines.speaker: Learner
lines.text: Wait — I have a fifty.
lines.th: เดี๋ยวนะ มีห้าสิบ

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Fifty, good. Twenty back for you. Take care.
lines.th: ห้าสิบ ดีเลย ทอนยี่สิบนะ เดินทางปลอดภัย

chunk_drills.label: Fare before you go
examples: How much to the bus station?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Recycles 'How much…?' from prices/shopping; adds destination with 'to +' place noun. Ask BEFORE getting on.

chunk_drills.label: Check the number you heard
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Rising-intonation confirmation question with no auxiliary; recycles numbers 13–90.

chunk_drills.label: Push back on the price
chunk_drills.pattern: That's a bit much. Can you do [number]?
examples: That's a bit much. Can you do forty?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: 'Can you…?' request form for negotiating; softener 'a bit'.

chunk_drills.label: Stop and steer
chunk_drills.pattern: Stop [here / at the ___], please. / Straight ahead, then [left / right].
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Polite imperative + 'please'; prepositions of place (at / after / before). Say it early, not at the last second.

chunk_drills.label: Paying and change
chunk_drills.pattern: Here's [amount]. / Do you have change for [note]?
examples: Do you have change for a hundred?
Sorry, I only have a five hundred.
I have a fifty — is that okay?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: 'Here's…' for handing something over; 'Do you have…?' recycled from shopping.

chunk_drills.label: Repair and clarify
chunk_drills.pattern: Sorry, could you say that again? / Sorry, how long? / How far is it?
examples: Sorry, could you say that again?
chunk_drills.spiralled_grammar: Recycled clarification set from greetings and directions units; use it instead of nodding.

listening_items.audio_text: Straight ahead, then left at the market — I can't stop on the main road.

guided_roleplay.learner_role: Passenger taking a motorbike taxi to the night market, then a songthaew back to the guesthouse
flow: Step 1 — Approach the driver and name your destination: 'Excuse me, how much to the night market?'
Step 2 — Hear the price and repeat it back to confirm ('Sixty, not sixteen?').
Step 3 — Settle the fare: accept, or ask 'Can you do forty?' Agree BEFORE getting on.
Step 4 — Sort out logistics: ask for a helmet, or ask 'Is this one going to the market?' for the songthaew.
Step 5 — Give the stopping instruction early: 'Stop at the front gate, please' / 'Straight ahead, then left.'
Step 6 — Pay and deal with change: 'Here's a hundred — do you have change?'
Step 7 — Close politely: 'Thanks. Have a good day.'
sentence_frames: That's a bit much. Can you do ___?
Sorry, could you say that again?

free_roleplay.ai_persona: A friendly, brisk local driver who works a motorbike-taxi stand and also drives a songthaew. Speaks short, simple English over engine noise, uses numbers fast, and does not repeat unless asked. Never hostile — just busy.
free_roleplay.a2_behavior: Gives a clear price when asked, confirms the number when the learner repeats it, waits for the learner to name a stop, and takes payment with correct change. Stays on the standard sequence: price → get on → stop → pay.
b1_curveballs: No change: 'Sorry, I can't break a five hundred — have you got anything smaller?'
Road closed: the driver can only get within 400 metres and gives walking directions the learner must read back.
Price goes up mid-ride: 'It's raining / you've got a big bag — make it eighty.'
Waiting game: 'We go when I have four passengers — maybe fifteen minutes.' Learner must ask how long and decide.
Wrong destination: the driver repeats a similar-sounding place ('the new market?') and heads the wrong way until corrected.
Number trap: the driver says 'thirty' but the learner hears 'thirteen' — payment mismatch must be repaired politely.

roleplay_rubric.criterion: Agreed the fare out loud BEFORE getting on or in
Repeated the number back to confirm it (e.g. 'Thirty, not thirteen?')
Gave a clear stopping instruction early enough ('Stop here, please' / 'Straight ahead, then left')
Handled payment and change, including a note that was too large
Asked at least one clarification question instead of nodding along
Register stayed casual-polite — short requests with 'please', no shouting or bare commands
Pronunciation: -teen/-ty numbers distinguishable and final consonants released in 'stop', 'left', 'right', 'front gate'
Stretch (B1): coped with an off-script problem — no change, closed road, mid-ride price change — and still finished the ride and paid

register_culture_note.en: Street transport English is short, friendly and loud enough to be heard over an engine. Full sentences are not expected — 'How much to the market?', 'Stop here, please', 'Thanks' is a complete, polite conversation. Two habits protect you: say the price out loud before you get on, and repeat any number back to the driver. Asking the price is never rude; it is what every local passenger does.

do_dont.avoid: Shouting just 'Stop!' at the last second
do_dont.prefer: 'Stop here, please' — said a few seconds early, with the final /p/ released
'How much to Big C?' then 'Can you take me to Big C?'

do_dont.avoid: Answering a price with a mumbled 'sixty' that lands as 'sixteen'
do_dont.prefer: 'Sixty. Six-zero.' — spell the number out when it matters

do_dont.avoid: Nodding and smiling when you didn't understand the detour
do_dont.prefer: 'Sorry, could you say that again?' / 'How far is the walk?'

do_dont.avoid: Getting on first and asking the price later

register_culture_note.thai_cultural_note: In many Thai towns the fare is posted at the motorbike-taxi stand or fixed by route for the songthaew, so passengers rarely need to negotiate or confirm anything out loud. Outside that system — in another country, or with an unfamiliar driver — silence is read as agreement, and a fare you never said aloud is a fare you can be charged twice for. The same goes for stopping: waiting quietly rather than interrupting the driver, out of consideration, is what leaves people standing a kilometre past their street. Speaking up early here is not pushy; drivers expect it and prefer it.

can_do_checkpoints.statement: I can ask how much a ride costs and agree the fare before I get on.
I can repeat a price back to check I heard it right (thirty, not thirteen).
I can tell a driver where to stop and say straight / left / right.
I can pay and ask for change.
I can negotiate a fare and ask about a per-person price or a wait time.
I can understand a detour or a drop-off change, ask how far I must walk, and read the directions back.
My -teen/-ty numbers are distinguishable and my final consonants in 'stop', 'left', 'right' and 'front gate' are clearly released.
